reviews.title: Lightrix Falling Behind
reviews.text:
I still consider Light Trix the best apps for phone media on the market. This includes their AI engine/models, which were some of the first to be made public for any app. 

However, in my opinion, not only is Photoleap still limited compared to the desktop version of Photoshop, but their AI function has deteriorated ever since it’s Genesis. Indeed, the AI quality and detail has improved, but its originality seems to actually be going downhill. The images it generates seemed far more conceptual and even innovative in the first couple of years of development than it has now become. In some way, Photoleap’s generative AI function used to take a lot more liberties than it does now. 

These days you see a lot more of the same type of image in different variations, even though it’s in greater detail than it once was. Back then you would see wildly different images from one to the next, even though indeed selecting the genre was still a part of the process. 

Both Photoleap and Videoleap are very expensive apps, and both are very limited for the money. Videoleap hardly seems to generate any AI at all, and both apps are difficult to see the quality of what you’re doing while working on the limited size of a phone screen. I don’t have a tablet, but I’m assuming it would be the same types of functionalities for them. 

But again, even more than the AI limitations are how limited the functions are when coupled with how small a screen I’m working with for both Lighttrix apps. I actually

reviews.title: DO NOT TRUST THIS APP
reviews.text:
I had a very bad experience with Photoleap. I hadn’t used the app for many months and had deleted it long ago. I also checked my Apple subscriptions and saw nothing active, so I genuinely believed everything was canceled.

Out of nowhere, I was charged again for a full annual subscription. No warning email about renewal, or anything. It turns out the subscription was made through their website, not Apple, and this was not clearly communicated. There was no obvious reminder, no clear warning, and no easy way to confirm cancellation.

When I contacted support, I only received automated, copy-paste responses referring me to their policy. There was no real customer service, no meaningful review of my case, and no clear confirmation that my account is fully canceled and won’t be charged again.

After reading other reviews here, it’s clear this has been happening to many users for a long time. If you’ve had a similar experience, I encourage you to leave an honest review and report it through official channels so this pattern gets proper attention.
The app may look professional, but the subscription and support practices are confusing and user-unfriendly. Please be extremely cautious before signing up — deleting the app or checking Apple subscriptions is not enough.
